statement.excerpt: Most recently, DeepSeek, which more or less matched OpenAI’s o1, accelerated those price wars, and OpenAI was forced (already) to drop prices.
statement.document_title: Five ways in which the last 3 months — and especially the DeepSeek era — have vindicated “Deep learning is hitting a wall"

from_speaker: more or less matched OpenAI’s o1
OpenAI was forced (already) to drop prices
our_interpretation: DeepSeek refers to its contemporary reasoning model R1, compared with the released o1 model.
More or less matched means broadly comparable performance on relevant reasoning tasks, not identical performance on every task.
Forced means DeepSeek materially influenced OpenAI's pricing decision; it does not require DeepSeek to be the sole cause.
A cheaper replacement offering can count as lower-priced access if its relevant capabilities are comparable. This is broader than a reduction in the same model's tariff.
The post's last-three-months framing bounds the historical causal episode.
The source specifies no model-specific price, currency, billing unit, or financial basis. Those omissions are preserved in metric_scope.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable reasoning evaluations and a dated reduction in comparable OpenAI access prices, together with credible evidence that DeepSeek materially influenced that decision.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that the relevant performance was not broadly comparable, that comparable access prices did not fall, or that the alleged pricing response was decided independently of DeepSeek.
